known_limitations: Behavioral cloning of the stateful Dragapult teacher into a <300k-param policy reproduces ~73% of test decisions but compounding errors collapse full-game strength (both students clearly inferior to the teacher; one-sided LB 0.085/0.125 << 0.45).

S2 GRU inference uses the student's own previous action count as an explicit input while training used the teacher's; a minor S2-only input skew. Immaterial to conclusions (S2 also ties S1 offline where inputs are matched). Documented, not retrained.
Exact competition size/latency limits and full rules text are not machine-retrievable (inherited from c005); size limit treated conservatively (100MB) and latency reported as single-process P99.
Engine trajectories are non-reproducible (std::random_device); the dataset/splits, offline eval, and checkpoints are reproducible; gameplay conclusions rest on statistical intervals over many games.
negative_result_note: A PASS does not require a successful student; it requires correct, honest execution and rule-anchored decision-making. Both students BEAT the deterministic control (learned to imitate) but are not teacher-strong.
